text.p: The Italian cash bond market staggered over the finishing line with mild gains in the penultimate trading session of the year while futures skated to the finish some 30 basis points ahead.
Traders said the gains were mostly due to the firmer dollar which was sustaining European markets. The lira held steady at 982.60/3.00 per mark from only a fraction weaker earlier.
The Italian cabinet wound up a meeting as the market was closing at which government sources said it approved a year end package of fiscal measures, the last part of the 1997 budget.

The March Btp future on LIFFE ended 30 basis points firmer at 128.55 while the July 2006 Btp was two basis points up at 108.75, yielding 7.58 percent and showing a spread of 180 basis points over the benchmark 10-year Bund.
Traders said they expected Tuesday to be quiet ahead of the year end, with a diminishing amount of players in the market for the holiday period.
